chapter_title: Concerning the Body: It was constructed after the

fills.notes: The body-to-cosmos mapping here requires the generative/active side corresponding to the productive earth below (the great earth as recipient/field). The transmitted editor fill fits the correspondential pairing (male = earth’s outward/productive plane in ultimates).

fills.fill: are appointed under the authority of
fills.notes: The syntax demands a mediating clause: after the Keeper of Splendour’s authority over the three heavens, the next level ‘below him’ must be described as subordinated, before naming the great King of Honour. Old substrate prefers structural/administrative language (‘appointed under authority’) rather than narrative or devotional phrasing.
Restores the parallel formula used in ¶7–10: ‘watch, of which X is master, his authority…’.
Required to resume the subject (the Adamant) and maintain the cadence of successive governing actions (‘his authority… And he invigorates…’).

The clause describes the watchers’ response to ‘earthquake and treachery’: correspondentially, a stabilizing resistance in the station of Honour. This also prepares the descent/humbling of those ‘who were sent’ (the corrective emissaries) by contrasting their action with the watchers’ stance.
The zodiacal signs are described as bound to the turning wheel; the natural correspondential action is fixing/placing them in their appointed stations on the sphere.
Immediately followed by ‘fixed, and planted’: the threefold fixation language commonly accompanies appointment to rule/order in the oldest cosmological register.
After ‘appointed and made leaders’, the substrate typically adds a functional title: guarding/keeping the ordered courses on the sphere (not moral exhortation).

fills.fill: in the head of Aries and in the tail of Pisces
fills.notes: The passage’s intent is to identify the sequence’s beginning and end (‘find the head… and the tail too…’). In zodiacal order, Aries is the head (first) and Pisces the tail (last).
The sentence compares the body-bent arrangement with how the signs occur ‘on the wheel … up’; the missing words must describe their motion/course upon the wheel.
The left-side count in ¶36 is said to run ‘from its hip to its head’; thus the first left member corresponding to Libra should be the left hip.

After ‘beset and destroy one another’, the next effect in the body should be interior wasting before eruption outward; this matches the correspondential movement from internal conflict to external manifestation (sores/boils).
The bracket shows traces consistent with a Coptic particle like ‘until’; the sense requires a temporal threshold leading to eruption from the dying body.
After ‘until they are squeezed … and the suppuration forced out’, the text expects an iterative adverbial phrase describing repeated pressing/expressing until emptied.

assessment: Most lacunae are formulaic and restore securely (titles, parallel governance clauses, body/zodiac correspondences). The harder points are the narrative mechanics in ¶13 and the pathological sequence in ¶39, where multiple readings could fit; restorations there follow the inside→outside correspondential logic (stabilization vs. treachery; internal conflict → external eruption → repeated discharge → healing) but remain tentative in exact wording.
